claims.text: A 5–10 nm Cu-compatible adhesion layer is to be deposited by ALD onto exposed surfaces of a connected W skeleton before Cu infiltration.
ALD at approximately 350 °C can produce a continuous, defect-free 5–10 nm adhesion layer on the W skeleton.
Conducting ALD in an inert or reducing atmosphere will avoid oxidation of the relevant surfaces.
Diffusion sintering near 800 °C under reduced-oxygen conditions will facilitate interdiffusion at the engineered W–Cu interface.
The adhesion layer will not be degraded by diffusion sintering near 800 °C.
The conformal adhesion layer will act as an atomic-scale bonding bridge between W and Cu.
The ALD-deposited layer will improve Cu wettability on tungsten.
The ALD-deposited layer will enhance interfacial diffusion between W and subsequently infiltrated or sintered Cu.
Improved interfacial transport and diffusion will suppress phase separation and microstructural inhomogeneity.
Improved wetting and interfacial diffusion will minimize void formation at W–Cu interfaces.
The engineered composite will have near-perfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
The engineered composite will have lower porosity than a directly Cu-infiltrated and diffusion-sintered control.
The engineered composite will have higher thermal conductivity than a directly Cu-infiltrated and diffusion-sintered control.
The engineered composite will retain greater mechanical durability under irradiation than a directly Cu-infiltrated and diffusion-sintered control.
Conventional direct Cu infiltration and low-temperature diffusion sintering of connected W skeletons typically suffer from phase separation.
Conventional direct Cu infiltration and low-temperature diffusion sintering of connected W skeletons typically produce interfacial voids.
The intervention is applicable only to configurations containing pre-formed, connected W regions.
The intervention is expected to remain effective at processing temperatures up to approximately 800 °C.
Scalability of the ALD treatment to large or complex W-skeleton geometries is not established.
Long-term stability of the engineered interface under fusion-reactor irradiation is not established.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes the connected W skeleton as already embedded within a Cu matrix, whereas the intervention and experiment require exposed W surfaces before Cu infiltration. The actual starting point is therefore inconsistent.
